newsitem.title: USA: NYCE cotton ends firm and near highs, trade light.
newsitem.headline: NYCE cotton ends firm and near highs, trade light.

text.p: NYCE cotton closed firmer and near the day's highs but volume remained thin at an estimated 5,100 lots, market sources said.
They expect light volume ahead of the U.S. Department of Agriculture's monthly supply and demand report, released August 14.
"I wouldn't take a big stance either way before the report and I'm no different than anyone else," Sharon Johnson, an analyst with Frank Schneider and Co Inc, said.
"There is nothing else to move this market."

But as players await the report and anticipate output around 18.2-18.5 million bales, many industry sources doubt the U.S. will actually produce that much cotton as the midsouth and the southeast suffers from a lack of rain.
Heavy rains early in the season put the crop behind schedule.

"The crop is catching up like a gangbuster but a lot of dryland cotton has to get rain," O.A. Cleveland, a cotton marketing specialist with Mississippi State University, said. "We should see a big (production) number but it will be difficult to maintain it."
The December contract closed 0.39 cent higher at 75.41 cents a lb, having ranged from 75.45 to 74.75 cents. The rest of the board closed 0.25 to 0.47 cent higher.
The benchmark December contract found support at 74.75 cents, just over Monday's low of 74.70 cents, after early fund selling.
The October contract closed at a 0.02 cent premium to December compared with a 0.05 cent premium in December on Monday.
